findings.summary: The two-way clustering formula is stated as standard errors adding linearly and subtracts a 'pooled' term, which is incorrect: variance matrices combine, not SEs, and the subtracted term is the team-by-time intersection, not the classical/pooled variance.
findings.evidence: Cameron-Gelbach-Miller (2011) two-way clustering: V_two-way = V_team + V_time - V_(team x time). Standard errors are not additive (only the variance matrices combine), and the subtracted term is the cell-level intersection cluster, not the 'pooled' (classical) variance. Suggested correction: 'V_two-way = V_team + V_time - V_(team x time) (the cluster variances add and the cell-level overlap is subtracted; SEs are the square roots).'
findings.verify_note: L570 formula 'SE_two-way = SE_team + SE_time − SE_pooled' is mathematically incorrect: standard errors are not additive. Per Cameron-Gelbach-Miller (2011) the variance matrices combine as V_G+V_H−V_(G∩H); the subtracted term is the team×time intersection cluster (which equals the White/robust variance in a one-obs-per-cell panel), not the classical/pooled variance. action=report; the finding's characterization and suggested correction are textbook-correct. Confirmed.

findings.summary: The ADL Key Concept callout mislabels the 2-month cumulative distributed-lag sum (0.78) as 'the long-run multiplier ... eventually transmits,' contradicting the chapter body which labels 0.78 the interim multiplier and the long-run/total multiplier ≈0.90-0.95.
findings.evidence: Chapter body L1208-1216 states 'After 2 months: gamma0+gamma1+gamma2 ≈ 0.78' as the interim multiplier and 'Long-run effect (total multiplier): ... coefficient ≈ 0.90-0.95.' The KC callout at L130 calls the same 0.78 'the long-run multiplier' that 'eventually transmits,' which both contradicts the body and is methodologically imprecise: for an ADL with lagged dependent variables the long-run multiplier is (sum gamma)/(1 - sum alpha), not the raw sum of gamma. (L1148 in the body carries the same loose 'eventually passes through' phrasing.)
findings.old: once $\gamma_1 \approx 0.20$ and $\gamma_2 \approx 0.08$ are added, the long-run multiplier is roughly 0.78 — meaning about 78% of a 1-year-rate shock eventually transmits to the 10-year rate.
findings.new: once $\gamma_1 \approx 0.20$ and $\gamma_2 \approx 0.08$ are added, the two-month cumulative multiplier is roughly 0.78 — meaning about 78% of a 1-year-rate shock has passed through to the 10-year rate within two months (the full long-run effect is larger).
findings.verify_note: KC L130 calls 0.78 'the long-run multiplier ... eventually transmits,' but body L1208-1216 explicitly labels 0.78 the 2-month interim multiplier and the long-run/total multiplier ≈0.90-0.95. For an ADL with lagged y the long-run multiplier is (Σγ)/(1−Σα), not raw Σγ. Fix relabels 0.78 as 'two-month cumulative multiplier' and defers the long-run to the body's 'larger' value — internally consistent. old string matches L130 (em-dash). Confirmed.
